headline: First vote passes 8-0 on data center moratorium until November 30th, 2027
summary: The moratorium would stop the city from accepting, processing, or approving data center applications, including building permits, special permits, and site plan approvals. The Planning Board voted 7-0 to recommend adoption, and a second vote and final passage come at the next regular meeting on the 23rd of this month. A $20,000 request to the mayor for the Human Rights Committee passed 5-3.
decisions: Approved 8-0 the resolution honoring finance director Bryant Ayles.
Approved 8-0 on a first vote the temporary moratorium on data centers, Order 250.
Approved 8-0 on a first vote a handicap parking sign at 21 Pond Street.
Failed 4-4 an amendment to raise Order 213 funding to the mayor's original FY '27 amount.
Approved 5-3 a request asking the mayor to raise and appropriate $20,000 for the Human Rights Committee.
Approved 8-0, with conditions, National Grid petition 31234447 for work on Bow, Wallace, Cabot, and Abbott Streets.
discussion: Data center moratorium: Speakers at the hearing supported the moratorium and urged the city to consider making it permanent, and one speaker asked whether a data center could be a public utility. The planning director said the state is expected to issue guidance at the end of the year, so the city wants time before writing rules.

Human Rights Committee funding: Members debated whether to fund the $20,000 request or restore the mayor's original amount, possibly $62,120. Some raised concerns about spending after the June budget vote, while others said the work should continue; the city solicitor said the money would still be subject to state procurement laws.

Flock camera surveillance: Public speakers urged the city to pass a surveillance moratorium and a Community Control Over Police Surveillance ordinance. A public speaker said the Flock contract expires this Friday, November 3rd, and asked what happens after that.
Beverly Farms library: A public speaker raised the probable closure of the Beverly Farms Branch after the next fiscal year's budget and asked that any remaining resources fund the dental clinic.
